Real cases

Three losses you only see on the invoice.

Real cases from Polish carriers, and what FleetPartner does about each.

  1. 01A real case

    The fault that sank in WhatsApp

    A driver reports a fault on WhatsApp. It sinks under other messages. A week later the truck stops in France: 2,000 EUR for the tow alone. The repair costs four times what it would at your base.

    With FleetPartner: the driver reports it in the app, with a photo. It goes to you, then to the mechanic, with a deadline. A counter shows the days it waits; a fault that comes back raises a warning.

    Count it in your numbers
    Fault reported Day 1Day 2Day 3 Repeat fault: warning

  2. 02A real case

    Lost hours leave a trace

    The plan says how far the truck should get. The log says what was declared. The tachograph says what happened.

    With FleetPartner: plan, log and tachograph side by side: unused driving time, overlong breaks, kilometres not driven. Not to punish anyone: to talk numbers, and fix it before BAG or ITD does.

    Count it in your numbers

  3. 03A real case

    Your workshop, counted in złoty

    A repair planned for 3 hours takes 5. Nobody counts it, so nobody sees it.

    With FleetPartner: every overrun counted, with what it cost. And the answer most owners can't calculate: is your own workshop cheaper than outsourcing?

    Count it in your numbers
    Planned: 3 h
    Actual: 5 h
    2 h over plan, in złoty

What FleetPartner doesn't do

  • Doesn't find loads. We connect your freight exchange or forwarder, free.
  • Doesn't replace your accountant. Your accountant gets a summary instead of a box of files.
  • No engine reader of its own. If your GPS has engine data, we connect it, free.

Other systems connect free of charge, once you get the data access from your supplier.

Sound familiar?

The problems carriers talk about, and what FleetPartner does about each.

Everyone calls me about every little thing.

Put what drivers usually ask into the order's remarks: where to refuel, the card PIN, unloading hours, how to load. The driver reads it in the app instead of calling you.

Where: Orders → Remarks

Orders get lost in WhatsApp.

Each order is entered once, with every point, the address checked on the map, deadlines and remarks. The driver, forwarder, office and you see the same progress.

Where: Orders · Addresses

Five points on the route, and I don't know which are done.

The driver confirms each point in the app, and you see it at once. No more "loaded? unloaded?". A changed or removed point needs the driver's confirmation.

Where: Driver's app → order → confirm point

My drivers are from Ukraine. Writing to them is hard.

The chat translates itself: you write in Polish, the driver reads in their language, and back. The app is in Polish, English, Czech, Ukrainian and Russian.

Where: Chat

I don't know if they did what I asked.

Give it as a task: who, what, and a deadline with day and time. "Wash the truck", "take the straps from the warehouse". You see when it's done.

Where: Tasks → Add task

The client calls every three hours: where's my load?

Send them a secure link. They see the vehicle's position, the order status and the estimated delivery time themselves.

Where: Dashboard → Share cargo

I don't know if the truck drives the way we agreed.

The live map shows every truck and compares the planned route with the actual trip. A deviation from the planned route raises an alarm.

Where: Live map

Twenty minutes late on Friday, stuck until Monday.

Every route is planned day by day: driving, breaks and rests, within the rules. Delays shift the plan, so delivery dates stay realistic and you see trouble early.

Where: Schedule

I can't remember loading times for 20 drivers.

You don't have to. The system watches every point's time and the driving plan, and shows only what needs a call: an unconfirmed point, a driver behind plan.

Where: Main dashboard → Requires response

By Friday, a whole day is missing.

Time leaks show unused driving, overlong breaks and kilometres not driven, by day. Plan, log and tachograph side by side: numbers for a conversation, not a punishment.

Where: Log → Time leaks

BAG or ITD finds the errors before I do.

Upload the driver card or vehicle file on the web. The analysis shows violations, gaps, driving without a card and the estimated fine, before an inspection does.

Where: Tachograph → analysis

Who's free, who's on holiday, who's still on the road?

The schedule shows routes, holidays and absences for the whole team, and each driver's driving time left this week and next. When a driver finishes, you know.

Where: Schedule · Log → Driving time

I found out about an expired inspection during a check abroad.

Every vehicle and driver document has its date in one place, with reminders before it expires. Road cards and the tachograph analysis download in one click for an inspection.

Where: Expiry dates · Road cards

Does my own workshop pay off?

Enter your mechanic's hourly cost and an outside rate. The report compares planned and actual time for each repair and shows what the same work would cost outside.

Where: Reports → Mechanics

A driver reported a fault, and it got lost.

The fault goes from the driver's app to you, then to the mechanic, with hours, deadline and budget. A counter shows days waiting; a repeat within 3 months raises a warning.

Where: Report a fault

After a driver change: who damaged the truck, and when?

A handover protocol with photos, the fuel gauge, equipment and remarks, confirmed by both sides and compared with the previous one. It stays on the vehicle's card.

Where: Driver's app → Handover protocol

The truck burns more than it should.

Consumption is calculated against each truck's own norm, and a rise reaches you as an alert. Incomplete refuellings are flagged. Set extra percent for mountains or city per order.

Where: Fuel

Calculating fuel takes my evenings.

The driver enters litres, odometer and a receipt photo when refuelling. The office fills in missing prices. Cost and consumption per truck are calculated for you.

Where: Road card → refuelling

The paper CMR travels three weeks in the cab.

The driver photographs the signed CMR at unloading. The office invoices the same day and confirms when the original arrives. The payment term starts from today's invoice.

Where: Driver's app → confirm unloading

The client hasn't paid, and I keep carrying their goods.

Give each client a credit limit. An order for a client in arrears or over the limit needs your conscious OK. A payment reminder goes out in one click.

Where: Clients → client card

I remember a debt only when there's no money for fuel.

The dashboard shows money coming in over 7, 14 and 30 days, and every overdue invoice.

Where: Main dashboard → Inflow forecast

Which runs and clients actually make money?

Every order, client and truck has its margin: fuel, tolls, empty km, driver, service, damage, fines and fixed costs. Sort the loss-making ones first, and see each cost's source.

Where: Profitability → Order profitability

What about KSeF?

Ready. Sales invoices go to KSeF from FleetPartner, and purchase invoices come in from it, without retyping. On euro invoices, the NBP rate fills itself.

Where: Invoices → Send to KSeF

A complaint comes in, and nobody knows who's handling it.

Each complaint has the client, order, amount, deadline and the person responsible, with its full history. Internal complaints from your employees too.

Where: Complaints

How much does a driver really cost me?

Reports show each driver's cost per kilometre, damage, fines and punctuality. Per diems, the foreign-work supplement and payroll are calculated from the same work and route data.

Where: Reports → Drivers · Payroll and per diems

Fines and damage: who is at fault, and what did it cost?

Every fine and damage has its driver, vehicle, date, amount and responsibility. The driver's history shows them, next to kilometres, orders on time and fuel.

Where: Report event → Fines or Damage

Who deserves a reward?

Ratings come from records, not sympathy: kilometres, damage, orders on time, fuel use, the truck's condition at handover. Set a competition with a prize; the ranking counts itself.

Where: Create competition

I'm afraid to give staff an account: they'd see our finances.

Each role sees only its part, and you switch permissions per person. Your dispatcher doesn't see finances. Someone you trust can accept service reports in your place.

Where: Employees → Permissions

Can your administrator see my clients and rates?

No. Your entries are encrypted, and nobody sees them, not even our administrator, unless you switch access on in Help. Every administrator login is recorded; ask for the report.

Where: Help → Administrator access

Do I need GPS devices in the trucks?

Most carriers don't: position comes from the driver's phone. Real-time GPS and the full driver and vehicle route history are available within FleetPartner. Need engine, fuel-level or temperature data? Keep your GPS hardware.

Can I keep my accountant or bureau?

Yes. FleetPartner doesn't replace your accountant. They work from one record instead of a box of files.

Can it connect to my fuel card, GPS or freight exchange?

Yes, free of charge, once you get the data access from your supplier: fuel cards, GPS (engine data included, if your GPS has it), freight exchanges, forwarders.

Is this going to be another job for me?

No. We set it up with you, show your drivers the app, and check every week for the first 30 days that everyone is recording. A guide on your dashboard shows each next step.

Can I buy just part of it, like the map?

No. A system that sees part of your company can show you the wrong picture. Every plan is the whole system.

Does it work on my phone? On an iPhone?

Yes, on Android and iPhone: the same system as the web. Get it on Google Play or the App Store. You buy the subscription and upload tachograph files on the web.

Does it find loads or plan routes?

It doesn't find loads, but we can connect your freight exchange or forwarder free of charge. Routes, yes: each one is planned day by day within driving-time rules.

Can I try it first?

Yes. The demo takes about 20 minutes. After that you get 30 days to test FleetPartner free of charge. No commitment.

What does it cost?

Per truck per month, net, the whole system.
